Vermiculite check — if present: STOP, photograph from hatch, disturb nothing, flag suspect ACM
Sheathing condition captured: staining, frost, daylight
Insulation depth measured with ruler in frame
Bath/kitchen/dryer ducts actually exit the attic
Vents open/closed appropriately for season and type
Every downspout pinned at its discharge point
Windows/doors from outside: sills, flashing, seal fog
Chimney pinned: cap, crown, flashing, mortar
Electrical service entry, mast, meter captured
AC/heat pump pinned: level, clearance, line insulation
Where water goes: swales, ditches, culverts
Septic lids and bed area pinned; surface condition
Bed area: nothing parked, built, or deep-rooted
Retaining walls pinned: lean, drainage, condition
Shoreline/dock captured; erosion comparison positions established
Outbuildings identified; each gets a zone if substantial

Ceilings below every wet room re-checked **after** all fixtures were run
Every interior exhaust (bath fans, hood, dryer, HRV) matched to a pinned exterior termination
Intake-declared property flags confirmed or corrected on site
Wood-burning appliance pinned and WETT flag recorded

Observed running through a heat call

Bucket test run — pumps, discharges, shuts off

Consumable size and last change recorded

Identified and traced to interior source

messages.text: Any idea why there’s no power to this

That's a basic flush-mount ceiling fixture with what looks like a small pull-chain knob on the bottom edge — see that little nub just below center? If so, this fixture may not be wall-switch controlled at all; it could be a pull-chain-operated fixture, which would explain why you're not finding a wall switch for it.

A few other possibilities worth ruling out:

- The wall switch could be controlling a different outlet/receptacle in the room instead of this fixture (common in older bedrooms — "switched outlet, no ceiling light" setups get mixed up).
- There could be a switch elsewhere you haven't spotted yet — check both sides of the doorway and near the closet.
- If there genuinely is no switch and no pull chain, the fixture may be dead-ended or on an abandoned circuit.

Worth a closer shot of that pull-chain knob, and maybe a photo of any switches on the walls near the door so you can match them up? If it turns out there's no control mechanism at all, that's worth noting for an electrician to trace out.
